modifiers.note: Authored tuning, not historical rates. Positive edge improves intimidation, aim and escape. Experience also gives a smaller bonus to going unnoticed; party condition never does.

reports.note: Authored tuning. Word of an incident leaves with its living local witnesses' contacts after a short delay and travels along the road with other parties and traders in both directions. Not a measured historical rate.

companions.note: Authored tuning, not historical rates. Bonds are drawn once per new journey for each pair of companions (at most one partner each). Attacks on a companion use the leader's shot plus willing helpers; companions close to the target fight back if bold, otherwise flee with what they can carry. Betrayal: each night a Ruthless or Opportunistic companion at their betrayal point may turn on the party (daily). The Ruthless, if willing to kill, shoot the leader first (ambush_hit, less guard_step for each companion willing to defend). Others rob the stores; each other companion may wake (notice) and stop it. Whoever succeeds takes the shares of food, cash and bullets; the betrayer leaves either way.

remains.note: Authored tuning. A wrapped adult body is counted as 150 lb of cargo; at most two ride with the party. Burying or opening a grave takes a day. A stranger killed by the party may carry a little money. Companions close to someone whose grave is opened take it as a grievous wrong; others mind less, and the callous not at all. Butchering takes a day and yields 40 physical lb of meat, valued by the ordinary meat food conversion, a deliberately modest game value with no claim to anatomical accuracy; it spoils and dries like other meat. In secret, each companion has a 35% chance to see it. Someone served it without being told has an 8% chance each day to find out.

kansas_river.title: The ferry landing
kansas_river.note: An authored encounter with a ferry crew, not a reconstruction of the Papin family or their Kanza relatives. A ferry taken from its crew must be worked by the party, with a higher mishap risk than a crewed crossing.

fort_kearny.title: The commissary tent
fort_kearny.note: An authored encounter at the new army post while soldiers build it (from June 1848), not a reconstruction of named officers or units. The only army post on the 1848 road. Soldiers close in fast: a failed escape becomes a standoff in which the party must surrender or shoot its way out.

pursuit.note: Authored tuning. After a party escapes the post, a few soldiers may ride after it for several days, once, while any are left who are not the commissary sergeant.

passing_traders.title: Passing traders
passing_traders.note: A template for every small trading party met on the road. Each party, named by its market window, gets its own lead trader, packer and armed hand when first targeted. Authored people, not reconstructions; food matches their three 50 lb trade lots.

passing_emigrants.title: An emigrant camp
passing_emigrants.note: A template for the other emigrant families camped near the road; each camp, named by its place in the journey, gets its own people when first targeted. Authored people, not reconstructions. They are armed and travel in company, so threats work less often than at a store, but nobody can hold the party long.

posse.note: An authored encounter, not a named historical group.

independence.title: The Independence general store
independence.note: An authored general store in the Missouri outfitting town, available when returning. Staff identities, stock and crime odds are gameplay estimates, not a reconstruction of a named historical shop.

unarmed.note: Authored close-combat risk; never consumes ammunition. Applies to a chosen unarmed attack, even with ammunition available.

wanted.note: Authored frontier-justice game rules, not measured historical probabilities. Missouri authority ends at the state line; regulators and rewards are extrapolations from emigrant accounts.

detention.note: Authored custody rules, not a historical sentencing table. Jackson County had a brick jail from 1841 and Missouri's penitentiary opened in 1836; Fort Kearny's guard holds offenders only once the post exists (June 1848); elsewhere an emigrant company tries its own. A Native household's kin bring a captured offender before their own council (see council). Hearing days, conviction odds, bail and jail-day rates are game estimates. See docs/FRONTIER_DETENTION_RESEARCH.md and docs/NATIVE_JUSTICE.md.

council.note: Invented for the game. No source consulted gives 1848 penalties for these communities, so these are authored game rules, not customary law. Theft: the goods' value twice over (return plus as much again). Robbery or assault: three times the value, never less than the minimum, and the council drives the party out of that country. A killing: the family chooses between a heavy price and the killer's life. Payment is taken in cash first, then goods; it never wipes out what others have heard.
